title: Release Campfire Notes — staffing heuristics & smoke scripts (Sep 2027)
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight working note (campfire-style) to capture staffing heuristics, a compact D-7..D+2 rollout cadence, and terse smoke-test scripts for the upcoming inference-router release. Intent: quick, readable, and actionable for on-call + release crew.

Scope: inference-router v2.3.0 — model routing fallback, prefix cache change, and telemetry sampling refactor. Non-goals: schema changes to client SDKs, long-term capacity modelling.

High-level timeline (compressed calendar):
- D-7 (2027-09-19): Preflight sync — owners confirm tickets, telemetry flags created, canary infra reserved.
- D-5 (2027-09-21): Integration smoke run against staging, verify KV cache hit-rate baseline.
- D-3 (2027-09-23): Canary config baked (10% routing), brief canary observers, schedule 2h monitoring window.
- D-1 (2027-09-25): Final go/no-go review, coms draft to #release-ops and infra pager.
- D (2027-09-26): Gradual traffic shift: 0->10% (30min), 10->50% (1h), 50->100% (1h) with holdpoints and automated rollback triggers.
- D+1 (2027-09-27): Post-deploy sampling + reduced throttling; followup smoke; first-day regressive checks.
- D+2 (2027-09-28): Cleanup: remove temporary flags, update runbook notes, retro scheduling.

Staffing heuristics (minimum crew by role):
- Release lead (1): single point of decision. Must be available D-1 through D+1.
- Observability lead (1): owns dashboards, alert thresholds, and trace sampling.
- SRE / infra (1-2): capacity and autoscaler monitoring; handle node replacement.
- Runtime engineering (1-2): rollback ownership and hotpatches for model-routing & cache code paths.
- QA / test lead (1): smoke acceptance and gating.
- Comms (1): posts to Slack channels, customer notifications if needed.
- Secondary on-call (1): backup for nights (if rollout crosses midnight).
Heuristic notes: total crew 5–8 people for a mid-size change. If the change touches storage/kv, +1 infra is recommended. If latency SLO is close to margin, add extra SRE.

Shift rotations (recommended):
- 4-hour focused windows for each person during D (staggered).
- Release lead covers D-1 09:00–12:00 and D 09:00–17:00.
- Observability covers D 08:00–midnight.
- If escalation occurs, rotate in the secondary on-call after 2h sustained pager.

Compact smoke-test scripts (run order: quick -> deep):
1) quick-health.sh (30s) — checks live endpoints and basic routing
- curl -sS -f https://router-staging.internal/_health || echo "HEALTH FAIL"
- check per-region endpoint (us-west, eu-central)
2) model-routing-smoke.py (2–5m) — verifies fallback selection logic
- run 100 requests with routing hints; assert >=95% successful fallback when primary unreachable
3) kv-cache-check.py (3–7m) — exercise prefix cache behavior
- write known prefixes, issue long sequences; compare cache hit rate to baseline (>60% after warmup)
4) latency-benchmark (5–15m) — tail-latency probes at target qps
- script: vegeta or wrk scenario at 20% of peak; record p95/p99, compare to SLO.
5) telemetry-sanity.sh (1–3m) — ensure traces and sampling flags flowing
- verify events in the telemetry sink for sampling-rate=0.1 flag; confirm trace ids in trace viewer.
Add to quick checklist: run quick-health and telemetry-sanity immediately after each traffic step. If either fails, initiate rollback.

Automated rollback triggers (pre-agreed):
- sustained p99 latency increase > 40% above baseline for 10m
- error-rate (5xx) > 3% for 5m
- KV cache invalidation rate > 20% (indicates corruption/regression)
- telemetry ingestion drop by >50% for 10m (blind spots)
Rollback path: immediate traffic reweight to previous stable version (automated via routing-control), then alert runtime engineering for hotpatch.

Telemetry experiments (during canary and D+1):
- Sampling plan: enable full traces for 1% of requests; increase to 5% during canary holdpoints if debugging needed.
- Tagging: add release-tag=rv2.3.0 on per-request metadata to filter traces.
- Quick metric diffs: compare p50/p95/p99, error-rate, routing-fallback-count, cache-hit-rate, and telemetry-ingest-latency.
- Hypothesis (to test): new prefix caching reduces p50 by ~8% on long-seq workloads; will not affect routing fallback rates.

Known risks & mitigations:
- Risk: model-routing fallback misclassification under degraded network.
  Mitigation: keep fallback debug logs verbose during canary; short-lived higher trace sampling.
- Risk: KV cache resetting on node churn.
  Mitigation: D-5 staging churn test; ensure warmup scripts present.
- Risk: Telemetry spike causing ingestion throttles and blind spots.
  Mitigation: ramp sampling slowly; watch ingestion quotas, pre-reserve burst allowance with observability team.

Open questions (needs answers before D-1):
- How long should we keep verbose fallback logs on in prod if no issues? (suggestion: 48h post-deploy then step down)
- Can release-ops authorize a 90-minute maintenance notification window for enterprise tenants? (Ravi to confirm with GTM)
- Is there a soft-capacity limit for dedicated customers that would trigger cross-tenant backpressure? (Infra to confirm)

Action items (short):
- Marisol: finalize canary config and post to #release-ops by 2027-09-21 (JIRA REL-2143).
- Ethan: add prefetched-key warmup to CI staging job by 2027-09-22 (PR: #8142).
- Lena: prepare telemetry dashboard clones and alert runbooks by 2027-09-23.
- Ravi: confirm enterprise notification window and add to comms template by 2027-09-23.

Post-release notes template (fill during D+1 retro):
- Summary: what shipped, brief bullet on rollback triggers, any deviations from plan.
- Metrics snapshot: p50/p95/p99, error-rate, cache-hit-rate before/after.
- Incidents: list and severity.
- Follow-ups: tickets and owners with target dates.

Notes to self: keep this doc terse; move detailed runbook fragments into release-runbooks/cutover-templates when stabilized.

Slack channels: #release-ops, #infra-oncall, #observability. Pager escalation: SEV for p99 spike -> paging policy (see Confluence link).

Quick references (tickets & PRs):
- REL-2143 (canary config), REL-2198 (kv-cache cleanup), PR #8142 (staging warmup), PR #8171 (telemetry-sampling).

End of campfire notes — keep this as the single source for day-of quick checks and staffing roster.
